Founded in [[Gurgaon]], [[India]], and legally domiciled in [[Bermuda]], Genpact employs more than 125,000 people and provides services to clients in over 30 countries worldwide. Genpact is listed on the [[NYSE]] and generated revenues of US$5.08 billion in 2025.{{Cite web |title=Genpact Ltd (G) Stock Price & News - Google Finance |url=https://www.google.com/finance/quote/G:NYSE |access-date= |website=www.google.com |language=en-US}} ==History== === Founding and early developments === Genpact was founded in 1997 as a unit of [[General Electric]].{{Cite web |title=Genpact (G) |url=https://www.forbes.com/companies/genpact/ |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=Forbes |language=en |archive-date=20 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520202213/https://www.forbes.com/companies/genpact/ |url-status=live }} The company was founded as GE Capital International Services (GECIS) in [[Gurgaon]]. Starting with 20 employees under the leadership of CEO [[Pramod Bhasin]], its charter was to provide business process outsourcing solutions to GE's businesses.{{Cite news |last=Bhasin |first=Pramod |date=2011-06-01 |title=How I Did It: Genpact's CEO on Building an Industry in India from Scratch |work=Harvard Business Review |url=https://hbr.org/2011/06/how-i-did-it-genpacts-ceo-on-building-an-industry-in-india-from-scratch |access-date=2022-04-04 |issn=0017-8012 |archive-date=7 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007210041/https://hbr.org/2011/06/how-i-did-it-genpacts-ceo-on-building-an-industry-in-india-from-scratch |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |agency=TNN |date=May 17, 2011 |title=BPO pioneer Bhasin quits as Genpact CEO - Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/bpo-pioneer-bhasin-quits-as-genpact-ceo/articleshow/8377252.cms |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=The Times of India |language=en |archive-date=13 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221213172243/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/bpo-pioneer-bhasin-quits-as-genpact-ceo/articleshow/8377252.cms |url-status=live }} In the beginning, GECIS created processes for outsourcing back-office activities for GE Capital such as processing [[car loans]] and credit card transactions. It was an [[Business process outsourcing to India#General Electric|experimental concept at the time]] and the beginning of the [[business process outsourcing (BPO)]] industry.{{Cite book |last=Yesudian |first=Suseela |title=Innovation in India: The Future of Offshoring |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan. |year=2012 |location=United Kingdom |language=EN}} One year after its launch, GECIS employed about 800 people and generated revenues of US$4 million.{{Cite web |title=BUSINESS TODAY |url=https://archives.digitaltoday.in/businesstoday/20060507/cover1.html |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=archives.digitaltoday.in |archive-date=31 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211231090701/http://archives.digitaltoday.in/businesstoday/20060507/cover1.html |url-status=live }} By 2001, GECIS operations had grown to 12,000 employees and the company began to manage a wide range of processes across GE's financial services and manufacturing businesses. [[Jack Welch]], CEO of GE at the time, said that GECIS was a key driver of GE's growth between 1998 and 2001, and was responsible for reducing operating costs by approximately US$1 billion. In 2003, GE reduced its stake in GECIS to 40% and sold the remainder to two American [[private equity]] firms. At the time of the sale, GECIS employed around 13,000 people in India and 4,000 people in the US, China, Hungary and Mexico, providing a range of solutions in areas such as finance and [[accounting]], [[Insurance claims processing|insurance claim processing]], [[IT management]] and [[technical support]].{{Cite web |title=GE takes back seat at back office |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/business/ge-takes-back-seat-at-back-office/cid/698971 |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=www.telegraphindia.com |archive-date=6 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406181310/https://www.telegraphindia.com/business/ge-takes-back-seat-at-back-office/cid/698971 |url-status=live }}{{Cite news |date=2004-11-11 |title=Out of captivity |newspaper=The Economist |url=https://www.economist.com/business/2004/11/11/out-of-captivity |access-date=2022-04-06 |issn=0013-0613 |archive-date=7 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007043723/https://www.economist.com/business/2004/11/11/out-of-captivity |url-status=live }} By 2004, GECIS oversaw around 700 business processes for GE that had migrated from the US to India, generating revenues of US$426 million. === Independence and international growth === In January 2005, the company became independent and started to serve clients outside of GE.{{Cite web |last=Rogers |first=Bruce |title=Tiger Tyagarajan Trains Genpact To Transform Businesses |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/brucerogers/2016/09/08/tiger-tyagarajan-trains-genpact-to-transform-busunesses/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=Forbes |language=en |archive-date=11 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220411155654/https://www.forbes.com/sites/brucerogers/2016/09/08/tiger-tyagarajan-trains-genpact-to-transform-busunesses/ |url-status=live }} As part of this transition, the company changed its name to Genpact for “generating business impact.”{{Cite web |date=2018-07-05 |title=Genpact signs deal with Durst to stay in current space |url=https://nypost.com/2018/07/04/genpact-signs-deal-with-durst-to-stay-in-current-space/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=New York Post |language=en-US |archive-date=11 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220411155654/https://nypost.com/2018/07/04/genpact-signs-deal-with-durst-to-stay-in-current-space/ |url-status=live }} Also in 2005, the company opened additional offices in India and by the end of the year, recorded US$493 million in revenue, with 15% coming from new global clients, and the remaining 85% from GE. In 2006, Genpact further expanded in India, the Philippines, Mexico and China.{{Cite book |last=Plunkett |first=Jack W. |title=Plunkett's Outsourcing & Offshoring Industry Almanac |publisher=Plunkett Research |year=2008 |language=en}} In August 2007, Genpact was listed on the NYSE under the symbol 'G'. The company continued to grow, opening offices in six additional countries that same year and launching a joint venture with the Indian company [[NDTV]] to offer outsourcing services for the media industry.{{Cite web|date=2006-03-29|title=Genpact - NDTV collaboration|url=https://www.filmibeat.com/television/news/2006/genpact-ndtv-venture-290306.html|access-date=2021-12-14|website=|language=en|archive-date=14 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214145128/https://www.filmibeat.com/television/news/2006/genpact-ndtv-venture-290306.html|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|title=Annual Report 2007-2008|url=https://www.ndtv.com/convergence/ndtv/corporatepage/pdf/AnnualReport2007-08.pdf|access-date=2021-12-14|website=NDTV|archive-date=3 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211103032344/https://www.ndtv.com/convergence/ndtv/corporatepage/pdf/AnnualReport2007-08.pdf|url-status=live}} In 2008, the company crossed US$1 billion in revenue, with 53% coming from clients other than GE. From 2010 onward, the company increasingly focused its operations and presence in Europe and the US. As part of its shift west, the company moved its headquarters to New York and in 2011, Bhasin stepped down as CEO and became non-executive vice chairman of the company.{{Cite news |title=Pramod Bhasin extract: Genpact Ltd. is an American information technology services, consulting, and outsourcing company headquartered in New York City, New York. Founded in Gurgaon, India, and legally domiciled in Bermuda, Genpact employs more than 125,000 people and provides services to clients in over 30 countries worldwide. Genpact is listed on the NYSE and generated revenues of US$5.08 billion in 2025.
